question: An engineer is implementing traffic monitoring for a server vNIC that is configured with fabric failover enabled. The requirement is for the traffic to be sent to an analyzer, even during a failure of one of the fabric interconnects. The analyzer is connected to unconfigured Ethernet ports on both fabric interconnects. Which configuration accomplishes this task?
options: Create two traffic monitoring sessions with different names, one per fabric. Connect an analyzer on each FI as the destination for the monitoring session local to the FI.
Create two traffic monitoring sessions with the same name, one per fabric. Connect the analyzer connected to FI-A as the destination for both monitoring sessions.
Create two traffic monitoring sessions with different names, one per fabric. Connect the analyzer connected to FI-B as the destination for both monitoring sessions.
Create two traffic monitoring sessions with the same name, one per fabric. Connect an analyzer on each FI as the destination for the monitoring session local to that FI.
theory: When a monitored vNIC has fabric failover enabled, its traffic can shift between Fabric A and Fabric B during a fabric interconnect failure, so a monitoring solution that only spans one fabric would lose visibility during a failover event. The fix is to create two monitoring sessions that share the same session name (so they logically act as one monitoring definition spanning both fabrics), each with its own locally-connected analyzer as the destination on its respective FI — ensuring that no matter which fabric is currently carrying the vNIC's traffic, a local destination is already configured to receive the mirrored copy. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Traffic Monitoring, Fabric Failover Considerations)
